To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The use of ICM-DNA in CCH is a reliable and reproducible method for the identification of aneuploid cells in CCH and that aneuploidity can be found in both benign and malignant CCH.
the use of ICM‐DNA in combination with light microscopy allows for the identification of aneuploid cells, and therefore the diagnosis of malignant hidradenoma, in the majority of cases.
the use of ICM‐DNA in CCH may be helpful in the identification of aneuploid cells, which are often associated with a more malignant clinical behaviour.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a new method of DNA analysis by ICM‐DNA, which is able to differentiate benign CCH from malignant CCH, and to distinguish between malignant CCH and other malignant tumors with clear cell differentiation.
the identification of aneuploid DNA content in recurrent clear cell Hidradenoma (CH) by image cytometry (DNA‐ICM).
the development of new, highly sensitive and specific diagnostic procedures for clear cell hidradenenoma, which are capable of detecting even small differences in DNA content.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of a DNA content of 3n or more is a reliable and highly specific diagnostic marker of CCH.
the presence of aneuploid cell populations in recurrent CCH is a strong indicator of malignancy, but the absence of aneuplodies does not exclude a malignant course of the tumour.
the identification of aneuploid DNA content by ICM‐DNA is a reliable marker for the distinction of malignant from benign CCH.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ICM‐DNA technique can be applied to the differential diagnosis of CCH and benign clear cell hidradeno.
we have developed a method for the detection of DNA‐aneuploidy in CCH by DMA‐ICM‐DNA and that this method may be a valuable diagnostic tool for the differentiation of benign and malignant CCH.
the use of ICM‐DNA in the diagnosis of CCH is of great value in the differential diagnosis from benign hidradenomas.
The main takeaway from our work is that

aneuploidity is a useful marker for the diagnosis of CCH, and the combination of DNA‐ICM with other diagnostic markers, including cytokeratin (CK) 7, 8, 18 and 20, and EMA, may help to differentiate between benign and malignant hidradenoma.
the DNA ploidy of the cells can help distinguish between benign and malignant clear cell hidracenoma.

the use of ICM‐DNA is a useful adjunctive diagnostic tool for the differentiation of benign and malignant CCH, as it can provide additional diagnostic information that may be useful in difficult cases.
